findings.text: Virtualization misc and time scaling ABI uses one enable at bit three, two extended enables at low positions zero and one, plus a time ratio interface with a high reserved mask and with minimum one and maximum spanning low forty bits and a unity default at one shifted by thirty two.
Logical AVIC entry ABI keeps guest identifier in low eight bits and reports validity through bit thirty one with a matching single bit mask.

Physical AVIC entry ABI places host identifier in low twelve bits and backing page address across bits twelve through fifty one, with log interrupt request near the top followed by running and valid indicators at the two highest bits, while table size stays within eight bits and doorbell and index limits use low twelve bits.

Unaccelerated access decoding uses low bit for write direction plus an offset field inside low twelve bits excluding low four plus a full thirty two bit vector field; delivery failure outcomes distinguish bad type from target not running from bad target from bad backing page from bad vector.
Physical identifier ceilings are 254 for legacy mode and 511 for extended mode and 4095 for the larger extended form.

Confidential paging feature flags use bit zero for active state and bits three through five for restricted injection and alternate injection and debug swap and bit nine for secure time, with an allowed features validity marker at the top bit of a sixty four bit word.
Segment record is a tight twelve byte entry holding selector with attrib with limit with base, using sixteen bit header fields then thirty two bit limit then sixty four bit base and no padding.

Classic save area begins with segment state for general and table and task selectors, then privilege level state, then extension state around efer, then control and debug registers with flags and instruction pointer, then stack and shadow stack controls, then system call state and fault address, then pattern and branch and exception records ending with speculative control, with reserved gaps preserving hardware offsets.

Encrypted save area extends classic coverage with per privilege shadow stacks and user CET state, plus extended control state around xss and xcr0, plus full debug addresses with masks, plus complete general registers, plus exit info and virtualization controls, plus time state around tsc scale and offset with tsc_aux and pkru, plus trailing floating and vector file covering x87 with mxcsr and xmm and ymm portions.

Guest host block pairs a sparse save area exposing selected control and pointer and general values with software exit descriptors and scratch and validity metadata around valid_bitmap and x87_state_gpa, padded to half the block, followed by a fixed shared buffer near two thousand bytes and trailing protocol_version with ghcb_usage and small reserved tail, filling one page.

Control block joins a fixed control prefix with a union overlaying classic host save state and encrypted host save state, so encrypted guests keep guest state in a separate encrypted page while this structure carries host state on transitions.

Layout stability is enforced at build time with classic save at 744 and communication save at 1032 and encrypted save at 1648 and control at 1024 with save offset equal to control size and whole communication block at page size, plus named reserved gaps pinned to stated hexadecimal offsets in each structure.

Processor identification uses an extended CPUID leaf ending in hex A, while segment attribute decoding defines shifts for system versus privilege versus present versus available versus long versus size versus granularity plus masks for type and for write with read alias and code access.

Event injection and exit reporting share low vector bits with a three bit type field and high validity plus error validity markers, covering interrupt and non maskable and exception and software types with a complement mask for reserved bits; task switch reasons use high shifts while register selection uses low four bits and selective control masking covers timestamp and emulation related flags.

Communication field helpers derive a bitmap index from field offset divided by eight and then offer validity test with raw fetch with guarded fetch returning zero while invalid and with storing setter that marks validity alongside value.

Each communication field starts invalid and transitions to valid on setter use and stays valid for later reads, with unchecked reads bypassing state while guarded reads expose zero until the valid transition has occurred.

Low level switch frame preserves callee saved registers with width dependent members and requires frame pointer with return address to remain adjacent for unwinding; fork frame nests that header above a full register snapshot.

Context switch is offered as a macro delegating to an assembly routine and reporting the prior task, while kernel thread startup initializes the switch frame by placing entry function with argument into designated preserved slots that differ by word width.

System entry refresh skips redundant work by comparing per CPU task state against thread state before updating task register and system entry register; stack update leaves trampoline pointer constant on thirty two bit and reloads stack top for paravirtual guests without fast return support on sixty four bit.
Synchronized bit helpers expose set with clear with toggle plus test and modify variants and a plain test alias, operating on volatile words with locked cycles and memory ordering.

Cross CPU bit safety relies on hardware locked read modify write rather than software spinlocks; callers retain responsibility for address lifetime and for higher level protection of multi bit invariants.

Core serialization prefers a dedicated serialize facility when available and otherwise uses an interrupt return to self sequence with distinct thirty two and sixty four bit forms; a pre usermode helper bypasses work when page table isolation already serializes and otherwise serializes immediately to cover later rescheduling.

Fallback serialization unmasks non maskable interrupts and runs slower than alternatives, while other serialization options may fault at low privilege or trap to a hypervisor, so callers must not assume timing or mask preservation.

Call number helpers read and write the saved original accumulator slot with rollback copying into live accumulator, error inspection examines live accumulator with sign extension for compatibility tasks, and return setup writes live accumulator preferring error over value.

Argument transfer differs by mode with thirty two bit order following base count data and index registers ending in base pointer and sixty four bit order following destination source data and extended registers, while compatibility tasks on sixty four bit use thirty two bit order; architecture query reports thirty two versus sixty four bit with extended thirty two bit tasks counted as sixty four bit.
Sixty four bit wrapper expands saved registers into ordered call arguments following native argument order for up to six parameters.
